impact: Body/status text at ≤55% white on the dark HUD backgrounds falls below 4.5:1. Specifically: `.hud-report` at rgba(255,255,255,.55) on rgba(10,4,26,.84) — this carries status/warnings/errors, so legibility is critical. Same class of problem: `.upload-face-label` (.55), `.sample-hint` (.45), `.detect-local-note` (.35), `.upload-license-note` (.3), `.detect-local-browser-hint` (.45). Lift muted-text opacity to at least .72 on dark, or introduce a semantic --hud-text-muted token calibrated for 4.5:1 against --canvas-bg. Errors/warnings (.hud-report .warn/.err) are already colored, so they're fine.
resolution: Committed in 3da65f6. Introduced three semantic dark-mode text tokens on :root (--dark-text-muted .82, --dark-text-dim .70, --dark-text-faint .60) calibrated against the ~#0c0620 effective HUD background (0.84 alpha over #1a0f2e), and swapped in the appropriate token for the six flagged classes: .hud-report + .upload-face-label (muted), .sample-hint + .detect-local-browser-hint (dim), .upload-license-note + .detect-local-note (faint). --dark-text-muted hits WCAG 4.5:1 body-text; dim/faint sit around 3:1 for supplementary meta only.
title: Multiple HUD text elements below WCAG 4.5:1 contrast
